edges.with: strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors (ketoconazole, voriconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin)
edges.mechanism: Inhibit CYP3A4 first-pass metabolism and P-gp efflux of sirolimus; ketoconazole raised sirolimus AUC ~500%.
edges.evidence: Phase I PK study in cancer patients; FDA label says avoid

edges.mechanism: Intestinal CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition; grapefruit juice raised sirolimus AUC ~350%. Label: do not take with sirolimus.
edges.evidence: Phase I PK study; FDA label

edges.mechanism: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor; single-dose diltiazem raised sirolimus AUC 60% and Cmax 43% with high inter-individual variability.
edges.evidence: Crossover PK study in 18 healthy volunteers

edges.mechanism: CYP3A4/P-gp induction; rifampin decreased sirolimus AUC 82% and Cmax 71% (CL/F up ~5-fold).
edges.evidence: PK study in healthy volunteers; FDA label

edges.mechanism: PXR activation induces CYP3A4 and P-gp; lowered tacrolimus AUC and caused cyclosporine-related rejection; same pathway clears sirolimus.
edges.evidence: Review of clinical interactions plus healthy-volunteer tacrolimus PK study; sirolimus-specific study not found

edges.mechanism: Cyclosporine raises sirolimus levels (dose sirolimus 4 h after cyclosporine); sirolimus increases cyclosporine kidney exposure and nephrotoxicity; cyclosporine augments sirolimus myelosuppression and hyperlipidemia.
edges.evidence: FDA label, rat PK/PD study, benefit-risk review

edges.mechanism: Additive angioedema risk (bradykinin pathway with mTOR inhibition); life-threatening cases reported; consider ARB instead.
edges.evidence: FDA label warning; cross-sectional series (15% angioedema on sirolimus); case reports

edges.mechanism: Immunosuppression may reduce vaccine response and allow vaccine-strain infection; label advises avoiding live vaccines. Non-live vaccine responses may be preserved or improved with mTOR inhibitors.
edges.evidence: FDA label; observational transplant cohorts; RCT in kidney transplant recipients

edges.mechanism: Sirolimus causes hypertriglyceridemia/hypercholesterolemia often requiring statins; label warns of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis with co-use.
edges.evidence: FDA label; MA of mTOR inhibitor metabolic toxicity

edges.mechanism: Metformin offset rapamycin-induced glucose intolerance in female mice and combination extended ITP mouse lifespan robustly vs historical rapamycin-alone cohorts.
edges.evidence: Mouse studies only; no human outcome data

edges.mechanism: Rapamycin plus acarbose started at 9 months gave longer male lifespan than prior rapamycin-only cohorts; both lower mTORC1 and raise cap-independent translation.
edges.evidence: ITP mouse studies only

edges.mechanism: Berberine inhibits CYP3A4; raised cyclosporine AUC 19% in healthy volunteers, so sirolimus exposure may rise similarly.
edges.evidence: Small human PK study with cyclosporine (n=6); extrapolated to sirolimus

edges.mechanism: Curcumin metabolites activated CYP3A4 and reduced everolimus (sirolimus analogue) AUC ~71% in rats; may lower sirolimus exposure.
edges.evidence: Rat PK and in vitro study; no human data

edges.mechanism: Herbal tea constituents inhibit CYP3A4 in vitro; a case of toxic sirolimus/cyclosporine levels after herbal tea; green tea extract itself did not extend ITP lifespan.
edges.evidence: In vitro and case-level evidence; no green-tea-specific sirolimus PK study

edges.mechanism: Quercetin modulates CYP3A4 and P-gp in vitro (acute inhibition, chronic induction); clinical effect on sirolimus unknown.
edges.evidence: In vitro review only

edges.mechanism: Overlapping mTOR/AMPK pharmacology; no PK interaction study found; resveratrol did not extend ITP lifespan.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic review and ITP mouse data

edges.mechanism: Label: may cause fetal harm; effective contraception during treatment and 12 weeks after; male azoospermia/oligospermia possible.
edges.evidence: FDA label

edges.mechanism: mTOR inhibition impairs fibroblast/angiogenic repair; wound complications 47% on sirolimus vs 8% tacrolimus.
edges.evidence: RCT in kidney transplant; critical review; label

edges.mechanism: Non-infectious pneumonitis 14% after late switch; risk with low GFR and troughs >12 ug/L; mTORi MAs show increased severe pneumonitis (OR 3.36).
edges.evidence: Single-centre series plus MAs of RCTs

edges.mechanism: mTORC2 disruption causes hepatic insulin resistance; mTORi raise hyperglycemia risk (RR 2.97); HbA1c rose with 1 mg/day in older adults.
edges.evidence: MA of RCTs, mouse mechanistic study, open-label pilot

edges.mechanism: Chromatographic and immunoassay sirolimus values are not interchangeable; troughs >15 ng/mL associated with hypertriglyceridemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia.
edges.evidence: FDA label; TDM cohort (n=150); PK review

edges.mechanism: True physiological rise in triglycerides and cholesterol (label 45%/43%); reversible on dose reduction.
edges.evidence: Label; case series; MA

edges.mechanism: Decreases in hemoglobin, hematocrit, MCV, platelets and lymphocytes even at low dose.
edges.evidence: Pilot RCT in older adults; phase I weekly dosing; open-label AD pilot

edges.mechanism: CYP3A5 non-expressers have higher dose-normalized sirolimus troughs and need lower doses; trough-guided dosing compensates.
edges.evidence: MA of 7 studies plus cohort studies
